images.title: Hand circle against round circle
images.purpose: Show that a circle drawn by hand comes out uneven when laid over a true round circle.
images.composition: One large circle centred with wide margins and a wobbly outline laid over it.
images.exact_structure: One perfectly round circle outline in teal #0072B2. Laid over it, one hand-drawn wobbly outline in reddish purple #CC79A7 that drifts outside the teal circle in 2 places and inside it in 2 places. Nothing else. Exactly 2 outlines.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any third outline, grid, or decoration
images.takeaway: A circle drawn by hand is uneven.
images.description: A teal round circle with a reddish purple wobbly hand-drawn outline laid over it, drifting outside in two places and inside in two places.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at where the two outlines do not match.

image_decisions.why: Laying the hand circle over a true one is a single picture that shows the unevenness.
